content.text:
Read the actual behaviour in `setup.go`. Here's my read.

## `--strict` doesn't earn its keep

The decisive fact: **the verdict never gates the work.** All five steps run unconditionally (`setup.go:2464-2468`); `ok` only decides the exit code and the closing line. So `--strict` changes nothing about what gets deleted — it only decides whether the exit code tells the truth. That's a very thin thing to spend a flag on.

Worse, it's already inconsistent with the command's own model. A **built-in** failure fails the command unconditionally *and* still deletes everything deletable. So "fail the command, delete what you can" is already the established policy here — `--strict` singles out external agents as the one class of failure whose exit code is opt-in. Nothing justifies that asymmetry: a leftover hook is a leftover hook.

And the flag is not free. It branches: the verdict expression (`!builtinProblem && (!strict || !externalProblem)`), the "not installed" early return (`setup.go:2433`), and two divergent warning texts — strict says "re-run uninstall", non-strict says "run the plugin command" — for the same underlying situation.

## The real distinction isn't internal vs. external, it's known vs. unknown

The genuine concern behind the non-failing default is different from the one the flag encodes. Discovery is ungated by design, so a crashed `entire-agent-*` binary on `$PATH` that has nothing to do with this repo shouldn't make uninstall exit non-zero forever, unfixable from inside the repo. That's a real hazard — but it's the *unchecked* case, not the *failed-removal* case.

You already drew exactly that line once: the "not installed" early return deliberately refuses to let unchecked plugins veto, precisely because discovery is ungated. Apply the same reasoning to the verdict:

| Situation | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Hooks were installed, removal failed (built-in or plugin) | **Fail** — positive evidence of a leftover |
| Couldn't check, our own agent | **Fail** — our own unreadable config is our bug |
| Couldn't check, third-party plugin | **Warn only** — no evidence anything is there, and it may be unrelated to this repo |
| Anything deletable | **Always deleted**, regardless of verdict |

## So: drop it

`entire disable --uninstall` should always exit non-zero when it knows Entire is still wired into this repo. `"Entire has been removed from this repository"` is simply false while a plugin's hooks are still calling `entire` on every agent turn — and the exit code is the only machine-readable signal a script or CI wrapper has. Making the honest answer opt-in means the default answer is a lie.

Non-zero exit isn't "blaming third-party code for Entire's uninstall" either — the report already names the agent and prints the plugin command. It says "this repo isn't clean yet", which is true, and it's attributable.

If someone ever does hit the unfixable-broken-plugin case, the escape hatch is the inverse flag (`--ignore-external`), added then, with a real report behind it. Not a flag shipped now to make the default output less accurate.

Net effect: one flag gone, the strict branch out of the early return, the verdict expression collapses to `!knownLeftover`, and the two warning texts merge into one (print the plugin command — the plugin binary may be the broken thing, so a bare re-run is the weaker advice).

Let me understand what the issue is, less words. Straight to the point

**The bug:** commit `39476dc6` made uninstall only call an agent's `UninstallHooks` if the sweep's `AreHooksInstalled` said "hooks installed". But those two functions don't cover the same ground:

| Agent | probe checks | removal strips |
|---|---|---|
| claudecode | 1 hook (Stop) | 6 hooks + `permissions.deny` rule |
| factoryaidroid | 1 | 7 |
| geminicli | 10 | 11 |
| cursor | 7 | 7 ✅ |

So if a repo has Entire hooks under `SessionStart` + `PreToolUse` but not `Stop`, claudecode's probe says "no hooks" → uninstall skips it entirely → prints "No agent hooks to remove", exits 0, deletes `.entire/`. Those hooks survive and now invoke an Entire that's no longer configured. Exactly the end state this branch exists to prevent.

**Why it regressed:** before `39476dc6`, built-ins were always asked to uninstall regardless of the probe — the probe was only for the confirmation summary. The comment that commit deleted said so out loud: *"it still removes hooks a stale AreHooksInstalled fails to recognize."*

**The fix:** the probe is fine as a *display* signal, wrong as a *gate*. Skip an agent only when (a) its check errored — already reported, already fails the command — or (b) it's a plugin that reported no hooks (subprocess, don't invoke third-party code speculatively). A built-in that cleanly reported none still gets asked: the call is in-process and idempotent, so it costs nothing.

**Two loose ends:**
- `TestRunUninstall_BuiltinNotDetectedIsLeftAlone` (`setup_test.go:1883`) asserts the regressed behaviour — it needs inverting, not just deleting.
- Output still says "No agent hooks to remove" even when a blind-swept built-in was actually cleaned, because the report line is keyed on the sweep's answer, not on what removal did. Matches pre-regression behaviour, reads wrong. Fixing it properly means `UninstallHooks` returning whether it changed anything.

That last one is the real design point: the probe should stop being load-bearing for both the gate *and* the report. Removal already knows the truth; it just doesn't say it.

No — the asymmetry is pre-existing on `main`. The PR didn't widen it; it made it load-bearing.

**Unchanged by this PR:** claudecode's probe was `hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.Stop)` before and still is. `UninstallHooks`'s removal set didn't change either — the branch only touched its error handling for an unreadable file. Same for the other agents: the branch changed `AreHooksInstalled` from `bool` to `(bool, error)` to separate "can't tell" from "none", nothing about what each one probes.

**What the PR changed** is how the answer is used. On `main`, `removeAgentHooks` calls `UninstallHooks` unconditionally for every agent, and `AreHooksInstalled` feeds one thing only — whether to print the "Removed X hooks" line:

```go
wasInstalled := hs.AreHooksInstalled(ctx)
if err := hs.UninstallHooks(ctx); err != nil { ... } else {
    if wasInstalled { fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Removed %s hooks\n", ag.Type()) }
}
```

So on `main` the narrow probe was harmless — cosmetic. `39476dc6` promoted it from a display signal to a gate on whether `UninstallHooks` runs at all, and a pre-existing gap became a leftover-hooks bug.

That's also why the fix is small and why the finding's framing is right: the probe was never built to answer "is there anything to remove", and the PR is the thing that started asking it that question.

input.message:
Task: plan a fix for a leftover-hooks regression on branch `fix/uninstall-external-agent-hooks` in /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/uninstall-ext (git worktree — run everything from there, do not cd to the main checkout). Please plan first; don't start editing until the plan is agreed.

## The bug

Commit `39476dc6` ("Stop reporting a successful uninstall that left hooks behind") changed built-in agents from "always asked to uninstall" to "asked only when the sweep reported hooks installed". But `AreHooksInstalled` asks a narrower question than `UninstallHooks` answers, so a clean "no hooks" is NOT evidence there is nothing to remove:

- claudecode: probes `Stop` alone; removal strips six hook types plus the `permissions.deny` metadata rule, which no probe looks at.
- factoryaidroid: probes 1 hook type, removal strips 7.
- geminicli: probes 10, removal strips 11.
- cursor: the only matched pair.

Repro: `.claude/settings.json` carrying Entire hooks under `SessionStart` + `PreToolUse` plus the deny rule, then `entire disable --uninstall --force`:

```
No agent hooks to remove
Entire CLI uninstalled successfully.   err=<nil>
still contains session-start  : true
still contains pre-tool-use   : true
still contains .entire/metadata : true
```

`.entire/` is deleted, so those surviving hooks now invoke an Entire that is no longer configured there — exactly the end state this branch exists to prevent. Confirmed a regression, not pre-existing: the identical case at `b5f141fe4` (the commit immediately before, on this same branch) returns false for all three.

## Why it's this PR's bug even though the asymmetry is older

I verified the probe/removal gap predates the branch — claudecode's probe was `hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.Stop)` on `main` too, and the branch changed only its signature (`bool` → `(bool, error)`, to separate "can't tell" from "none"), not what it inspects. `UninstallHooks`'s removal set is unchanged as well.

What the branch changed is how the answer is *used*. On `main`, `removeAgentHooks` calls `UninstallHooks` unconditionally for every agent and uses the probe for one thing only — whether to print a line:

```go
wasInstalled := hs.AreHooksInstalled(ctx)
if err := hs.UninstallHooks(ctx); err != nil { ... } else {
    if wasInstalled { fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Removed %s hooks\n", ag.Type()) }
}
```

So the narrow probe was cosmetic on `main`. `39476dc6` promoted it from a display signal to a gate on whether removal runs at all, and the pre-existing gap became a leftover-hooks bug. The comment that commit deleted named the hazard out loud: *"it still removes hooks a stale AreHooksInstalled fails to recognize."*

## Direction (a patch exists, verified — treat as a starting point, not a mandate)

Skip an agent only when either:
- its check failed (already reported, already fails the command), or
- it is an external plugin that did not report hooks — a subprocess, so don't invoke third-party code speculatively.

Keep asking a built-in that cleanly reported none: the call is in-process and idempotent, so it costs nothing.

That patch was verified: the three artifacts are removed, `go build ./cmd/...` and gofmt clean. The only failing test is `TestRunUninstall_BuiltinNotDetectedIsLeftAlone` (`cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go:1883`) — it asserts the regressed behaviour and needs inverting, not deleting.

## The open design question — please address it in the plan

The run still prints "No agent hooks to remove" while having actually cleaned a built-in swept blind, because the removal report line is keyed on the sweep's answer rather than on what removal did. That matches pre-regression behaviour but reads wrong, and reporting it accurately needs `UninstallHooks` to say whether it changed anything.

The underlying point: the probe is currently load-bearing for both the gate *and* the report, and it was built for neither. Removal already knows the truth; it just doesn't say it. Worth weighing whether the right fix is `UninstallHooks` returning a "changed anything" signal (and what that costs across all agents, including the external-plugin protocol) versus keeping the report imprecise for now with the gate fixed. Say which you'd pick and why.

Relevant code: `uninstallAgentHooks` and `getAgentHookState` in `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`, plus each agent's `cmd/entire/cli/agent/*/hooks.go`.

Repo conventions worth honouring: KISS/DRY/TDD (failing test first), tests assert the final positive spec — no narrating the journey or restating history in comments, and `mise run fmt && mise run lint` as a single sequence before anything is considered done.
